html:
The Mehmed Paša Sokolović Bridge is a stone bridge of eleven arches over the Drina River at Višegrad in eastern Bosnia, finished in 1577 by the court architect Mimar Sinan.

It was paid for by the grand vizier Mehmed Paša Sokolović, who had been taken as a boy from a Serb village nearby into Ottoman service and rose to rule the empire for three sultans. The bridge carried the road from Bosnia toward Istanbul. Ivo Andrić made it the hero of his novel The Bridge on the Drina, which tells four centuries of Bosnian history through it. The bridge was damaged in both world wars and became a site of killings in the Bosnian War. It is a World Heritage Site.
sum: The Mehmed Paša Sokolović Bridge is a stone bridge of eleven arches over the Drina River at Višegrad in eastern Bosnia, finished in 1577 by the court architect Mimar Sinan.
